cases.title: JSONP query callback must be a string before string replacement

pattern.observable_before: this.req.query yields a callback value that may be an object; if(callback) proves only truthiness, and the selected branch calls callback.replace without a string proof.
pattern.fixed_negative_control: After normalizing arrays, callback && typeof callback === 'string' dominates callback.replace; object values leave the JSON response unchanged.
static_requirements: Track the query-derived callback binding through the optional Array.isArray extraction.
Do not treat a truthiness guard as a string type guard.
Distinguish a recognized string-method receiver from an arbitrary object with a legitimate replace method.
pattern.not_a_general_rule: Do not flag every replace call without a local typeof check; known string sources and valid caller/type contracts are negative controls.
pattern.correctness_evidence: Original maintainer fix explicitly says the callback parameter can be an object; the separate regression test supplies that object-shaped query.
pattern.current_skylos_expectation: Not run or asserted; classify any detector result separately from this historical oracle.

caveats: The semantic type obligation comes from query/parser behavior and the regression test; syntax alone does not prove every arbitrary callback object invalid.

cases.title: OPTIONS response failures must reach the error continuation

pattern.observable_before: The callback has old(err) as its existing error continuation, but the no-error response-writing path invokes res.set(...).send(...) without converting a thrown error into that continuation.
pattern.fixed_negative_control: The same response work moves into a helper whose catch(err) calls next(err), and the completion callback supplies old as next.
static_requirements: Resolve the wrapped completion callback and its prior error continuation.
Model response-writing operations as possibly throwing under the known headers-already-sent trigger.
Follow the catch binding into the callback argument; a catch that discards or substitutes the error is not this negative control.
pattern.not_a_general_rule: Do not require try/catch around every call. The obligation is specific to this callback boundary and its error-continuation contract.
pattern.correctness_evidence: Original maintainer fix says an OPTIONS response-handler error caused a crash and references issue2494; the separate test establishes the headers-already-sent trigger and expected downstream middleware response.
pattern.current_skylos_expectation: Not run or asserted; this is a future contextual exception-flow oracle, not a claimed empty-catch detector case.

caveats: A missing local catch alone is not proof of a bug; callback ownership and the known failing response state matter.
